scenarios.hypothesis: The app recognizes a current owned session and rejects a private request without one.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: The synthetic owner reaches the workspace through the normal session reader. An anonymous browser is redirected to sign in.

scenarios.hypothesis: An authenticated owner cannot gain access to another company's private records by changing identifiers.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: Two synthetic tenants have persisted records. An owner cannot load the other tenant's project details or fetch its authenticated PDF.

scenarios.hypothesis: The owner can create, read, update and delete a client through the workspace.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: Browser interactions produce the expected tenant-scoped database state, including loss of access after deletion.

scenarios.hypothesis: The owner can edit an unaccepted estimate and recover its saved document content and totals.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: An edit survives a reload and renders in the public document with its original total. Chromium also exercises the paginated and full-width editor controls.

scenarios.hypothesis: An anonymous visitor with a valid estimate link sees the public document, and an invalid link fails safely.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: The anonymous document shows the seeded scope, line and total. Invalid-link handling produces the expected denial or not-found state.

scenarios.hypothesis: A recipient can sign the public estimate and recover the signed PDF.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: The app persists the signature and accepted state, and the PDF contains the agreed document data and signature evidence.

scenarios.hypothesis: An audio capture can progress through the actual app, API and Inngest handlers to a persisted estimate draft.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: Synthetic media enters the app and the draft renders in the workspace. Provider transports are simulated. The test makes no live AI or physical-device claim.

scenarios.hypothesis: The desktop description field prevents edits until its client handlers mount. A single replacement after mounting must persist exactly.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: The server-rendered field is disabled or read-only while client scripts are held. After mounting, native input events show the previous value fully selected and the exact replacement is saved in the database.

scenarios.hypothesis: An owner can create a manual project, rename it and permanently delete it from the Projects list.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: New Xtimate creates a new project and blank estimate. The title survives reload. The action removes exactly the new project and its estimate and preserves the fixture's original project.

scenarios.hypothesis: An owner can change the company display name and mailing address through the company settings form.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: The synthetic company row stores the new name, street, city, state and ZIP. A fresh page reload shows those values.

scenarios.hypothesis: An owner can create, edit, organize and delete a fixed-price service and its own Price Book category.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: The new service and category persist with updated names, price and assignment and survive reload. Removing the service and empty category removes their database rows and restores the empty state.

scenarios.hypothesis: A provider outage during text regeneration leaves the current estimate intact and offers recovery after Inngest exhausts its retries.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: Three scope-matched simulated provider failures produce a terminal generation journal event and visible Retry and Edit manually actions. The existing estimate stays current with its original total and lines, and the submitted description remains stored.

scenarios.hypothesis: A refused microphone permission gives the owner a recovery path without uploading media or changing the estimate.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: A simulated browser permission refusal shows the permission message, keeps Record enabled and allows Skip recording. No audio ticket, upload or recording is created and the prior estimate remains current.

scenarios.hypothesis: An anonymous signature created against a prior view cannot accept an estimate that the owner has since revised.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: The real sign endpoint rejects the original review timestamp and fingerprint with HTTP 409. No signature or acceptance is persisted, and the reload prompt displays the newly saved line.

scenarios.hypothesis: An authenticated dashboard, client list and editor expose named primary controls and fit the viewport in the required browsers.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: Each page has a full axe report and an impact breakdown for WCAG 2.0 and 2.1 A and AA tags. There are zero serious or critical violations. Locator checks verify accessible names and horizontal overflow.

scenarios.hypothesis: An anonymous estimate and its open signing dialog expose named actions and a viewport-fitting document.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: The document and open dialog have full axe reports with counts by impact and zero serious or critical violations under the selected WCAG rules. The signer's fields, consent action and cancel action have accessible names. These scans do not verify a keyboard alternative to drawing a signature.

scenarios.hypothesis: A keyboard user can open Add Client, understand required-field errors and resume from the same control after closing.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: Tab and Enter reach and open Add Client. The name has a label, required state and associated validation message. Escape closes the form and restores focus to its opener. The open invalid form also has full axe output with zero serious or critical violations.

scenarios.hypothesis: An owned workspace can render company branding, account, appearance, notification preferences and the team roster. Legacy settings URLs go to their current screens.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: Routing and rendering smoke only. Each final document returns HTTP 200 at the expected URL without browser exceptions, first-party server errors or horizontal overflow. The synthetic company name, primary fields, roster owner and documented invite preview are visible. Screenshots and navigation evidence are retained.

scenarios.hypothesis: Estimate settings, billing, integrations and knowledge screens render for an owned workspace, including the current destinations of legacy delivery and payment links.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: Routing and rendering smoke only. Each final document returns HTTP 200 at the expected URL without browser exceptions, first-party server errors or horizontal overflow. Default email and SMS switches are off and the disabled tenant has no pay-online switch. Message, client action, plan and credit usage, integration, and knowledge controls appear. Screenshots and navigation evidence are retained.

scenarios.hypothesis: The synthetic owner sees the empty notifications screen and Academy catalog. The retired chat base URL resolves to the dashboard.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: Routing and rendering smoke only. Each final document returns HTTP 200 at the expected URL without browser exceptions, first-party server errors or horizontal overflow. The notification filter and empty state, a course link, and the dashboard heading are visible. Screenshots and navigation evidence are retained.

scenarios.hypothesis: An anonymous browser can read the landing, sign-in, industry, publication, legal and offline fallback screens.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: Routing and rendering smoke only. Each document returns HTTP 200 at the expected URL without browser exceptions, first-party server errors or horizontal overflow. The sign-in controls, legal content, a sample industry, and either a blog card on the index or its empty state are visible. The offline fallback is rendered while online. Screenshots and navigation evidence are retained.

scenarios.hypothesis: Unsigned and forged Stripe, WhatsApp, Twilio and Telegram callbacks reject before business payload parsing, including malformed bodies.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: Each missing, forged and malformed unsigned callback returns 400/401 with a generic response. An invalid WhatsApp verification handshake returns 403 without reflecting the challenge. Payloads contain no real event or resource identifiers. This establishes rejection only; verified provider delivery and signed positive/idempotency tests remain separate gates.

scenarios.hypothesis: An owner can amend an accepted estimate with additional work and a credit; anonymous signed approval changes the contract total while preserving the original signed document.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: Actual original signing, owner draft creation/edit/persistence, owner-preview sharing, anonymous approval, frozen snapshot digest, public contract total 1225, unchanged base estimate/signature and semantic signed PDF. Approved editor fields are locked. No payment or outbound delivery is exercised.

scenarios.hypothesis: An anonymous customer can decline a shared change order without changing the accepted base contract or its signature.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: Actual original signing, owner draft/save/share and anonymous confirmed decline. Persisted change-order response is declined with no signature; public contract and project remain at 1000 and the original signature hash is unchanged. Owner sees the declined revision control.

scenarios.hypothesis: An authenticated ordinary tenant cannot read platform-admin pages or invoke the protected model catalog API.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: The actual session identifies the generated owner, admin API returns401 before provider access, admin navigation redirects through logout to sign-in, and the session becomes absent. Evidence contains only booleans and response statuses.

scenarios.hypothesis: A generated development platform admin can read the administrative dashboard, its own grant and company, scoped events and integration catalog.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: Grant only the marked random account when a non-QA admin already exists. Each core admin page returns200 with its expected controls, no uncaught exceptions or first-party HTTP5xx. No credentials are revealed and artifacts retain only sanitized states. Remove the exact marked grant during teardown. This does not establish administrative write/support workflows.

scenarios.hypothesis: Editing the quantity and decimal price of an existing line updates every persisted total and every document surface consistently.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: One UI replacement sets quantity3 and unit price125.50. Item, section, estimate and project total must equal376.50 with zero tax/discount. Reloaded width/page editor, semantic owner PDF and anonymous document show the same amount and original scope in all browser projects.

scenarios.hypothesis: An accepted signed estimate stays immutable to the owner and to a direct service-role line update; additions use change orders.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: Actual anonymous signing produces a snapshot digest. The owner sees Accepted and the change-order action, with no line edit controls. An update scoped to the marked account and exact company/section/item is rejected with P0022; line, signature and all totals remain unchanged.

scenarios.hypothesis: A generated branded link resolves by its exact short token while unknown tokens reveal no estimate.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: Real owner sharing opens the branded URL; anonymous access renders only the token document. Cosmetic prefixes do not authorize access; unknown or truncated tokens show no estimate fields.

scenarios.hypothesis: An owner can password-protect the estimate and anonymous access requires the correct password.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: A real saved hash gates HTML, metadata and PDF. Wrong password creates no cookie; correct password issues a Secure HttpOnly cookie and unlocks after reload over local HTTPS.

scenarios.hypothesis: An expired link discloses neither the estimate document nor its PDF.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: Only the synthetic estimate is seeded in the past. Both routes show expiration; token PDF returns410 and unauthenticated owner PDF401.

scenarios.hypothesis: A recipient can accept an estimate without a pointer by choosing a typed signature and explicitly submitting the existing consent.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: Actual Tab, arrow and Enter keys complete acceptance with zero pointerdown events. A600x160PNG, matching frozen snapshot hash and signer persist; the signed PDF contains the signer, scope, amount and image. Reload preserves acceptance.

scenarios.hypothesis: A recipient can approve a change order with only keyboard interaction and receive the same frozen contract and PDF evidence.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: After ordinary seller preparation, public Tab/arrow/Enter approval records no pointer events, persists the exact PNG and matching contract snapshot hash, updates project total to1075, preserves the original signature and renders the signed PDF after reload.

scenarios.hypothesis: A dedicated text-entry screen saves the exact description and generates the next current estimate.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: An initially disabled CTA enables after one exact fill. The actual202 request has manual_text lineage; the recording, successful pipeline event, version2/total1000 and anonymous generated lines persist.

scenarios.hypothesis: The photo-only screen requires its own uploaded photo before generating an estimate.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: A real browser file upload creates a scoped WebP object; photo lineage succeeds through Inngest, stores vision output and version2/total1000, and renders the anonymous document without creating an audio recording. Media/provider inputs are synthetic.

scenarios.hypothesis: A learner can complete a text lesson and see the resulting course progress after reload.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: The built-in text-only lesson generates actual tracked open and manual completion responses. The synthetic user's completion row and single completion event persist, and the course displays 1/3 completed and 33% after reload.

scenarios.hypothesis: A tenant owner can edit provenance and delete an indexed knowledge entry while another tenant cannot read it.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: A seeded synthetic vector is indexed. A real source-only edit persists without changing text or vector. A distinct authenticated tenant sees no row and the direct URL shows not found. The owner confirms deletion and the scoped database row is absent.

scenarios.hypothesis: A platform admin can find a specific failed attempt and see the actual failed step in chronological context.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: An exact synthetic attempt filter returns one row. Its details show the linked project, three ordered step and status pairs, and the expected synthetic failure code and message. Captures are disabled and the admin session makes no privileged UI writes.

scenarios.hypothesis: Invalid OAuth requests and unavailable invite paths fail locally, and owned users with a company land safely from onboarding and legacy password routes.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: Inline noindex OAuth and invite error states stay on the app origin. Disabled invite returns no token in its content and leaves membership unchanged. An existing owned account redirects from onboarding to dashboard and from update-password to account settings.

capabilities.reason: Real Google Identity consent, callback, new-account onboarding and recovery need dedicated test-account evidence. The owned session fixture starts after identity verification.
Delivery and callback evidence is missing for email, SMS and WhatsApp in approved provider test environments. Outbound delivery is disabled in the initial campaign.

Six isolated real Stripe TEST API/ledger cases pass, covering charges, duplicate/replay recovery, cumulative refunds, 3DS cancellation and subscription Checkout reuse. Hosted browser completion is under test. Signed callback delivery to the app HTTP endpoint and a complete browser-to-ledger journey still need fresh evidence; seeded invoice presentation cannot establish processing.
Approved live-provider runs for transcription and estimate generation need quality, timeout and failure-handling evidence. Local capture coverage uses simulated providers.
Real iOS Safari and Android Chrome still need microphone, camera, permission and interrupted upload evidence. Browser profiles exercise emulated devices.

Initial automated scans and client keyboard behavior have browser evidence. New keyboard-only estimate and change-order signing need fresh passing evidence; broader keyboard journeys and real screen-reader validation remain open. Automated rules do not establish WCAG conformance.

Scoped read-only admin pages pass all three browser projects; post-denial login is under retest after a canonical-origin fix. Administrative grant/revoke interactions, global configuration writes, support mode, audit records and the remaining admin surfaces still require isolated acceptance.
Seller creation, customer signed approval/decline and updated contract/PDF need clean evidence in all required browser projects. Invoicing and real payments remain separate.
A release candidate needs a smoke result from the actual release deployment and read-only public checks. Local Supabase runs establish development behavior.
